official.deadline_note: 27 March 2026 is the deadline published in the official Call for Applications for nominating agencies to submit the endorsed application forms; each nominating agency sets and communicates its own earlier internal deadline for applicants (Guidelines for Applicants, para 2.2.2), and postgraduate applicants were asked to apply for an HEI seat by end of January 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2026 edition (July/September 2026 intakes); annual call published by the Ministry, issued around October
official.status_note: The MASS page currently publishes the 2026 edition (Call for Applications, October 2025): nominating agencies were to submit endorsed applications by 27 March 2026, and host-institution application windows ran from October 2025 to March 2026 for the July/September 2026 intakes, so that round is now closed. No newer call is published yet; the scheme is an annual call, so the next edition is expected on the same page around October.
official.tuition_coverage_note: This scholarship provides for an annual payment of fees and other studies-related costs (e.g. general/annual fees/miscellaneous fees and laboratory consumables etc) as per the grid: SADC Countries - Local Fees - total fee payable up to MUR100,000; Non-SADC Countries - International Fees - total fee payable up to MUR160,000 (as at 25 August 2025, 1 USD = MUR 45.65). Fees and other studies-related costs over the amounts mentioned above shall be borne by the awardee.
benefits: Annual payment of fees and other studies-related costs (general/annual fees, miscellaneous fees, laboratory consumables etc): total fee payable up to MUR100,000 for beneficiaries from SADC countries and up to MUR160,000 for beneficiaries from non-SADC countries
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 credited to the awardee's bank account in Mauritius monthly, subject to the submission of evidence of attendance/progress in the study programme by the HEI
Return airfare by the most economical route, valid for travel from the country of origin at the beginning of the studies and back to the country of origin upon successful completion
The application fee of the chosen public Higher Education Institution refunded to successful applicants
Beneficiaries are entitled to free health care in public hospitals in Mauritius
The host HEI applies for the student visa and provisional entry permit with the Passport and Immigration Office before the awardee travels
eligibility: Candidates must be resident citizens of member states of the African Union or African Commonwealth countries; Mauritian nationals are NOT eligible to apply under this Scheme

Undergraduate applicants should be above 18 years of age and should not have reached their 26th birthday by 01 January 2027; MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD applicants should not have reached their 40th birthday by 01 January 2027
Applicants must have already applied for a full-time on-campus programme (Diploma, Degree, MPhil or PhD) at a public Higher Education Institution in Mauritius for the academic year starting in 2026

Bachelor's applicants: successful completion of end-of-secondary schooling with at least 21 points at GCE or HSC A-Level (A+=10, A=9, B=8, C=7, D=6 in three principal subjects) or at least an overall average of 60% or 12/20 equivalent to A level; applicants already holding an undergraduate degree, or a diploma for diploma entry, are not considered

MPhil/MPhil-PhD applicants: a recognised undergraduate degree with at least an upper second class degree (or CPA/GPA greater than 60%); direct entry to the PhD is allowed provided the requirements of the HEI are met

Self-financing African students already studying in Mauritius are NOT eligible to apply for the same programme level; scholarships are not awarded for top-up degree, foundation, part-time, distance education or mixed/blended programmes
requirements: Applications can only be made on the application form and solely through the nominating agency in the applicant's country of citizenship; Section 5 of the form must be endorsed and completed by that nominating agency
Obtain either a conditional offer (letter of admission) from the chosen Mauritian public HEI or a receipt of payment of the HEI application fee to submit with the scholarship application
Produce original educational certificates to the Ministry within two weeks of arrival in Mauritius; if qualifications are found not authentic, the scholarship is terminated immediately
Undergo a medical check-up in a public hospital within one month of arrival, as per Passport and Immigration Office requirements, with results submitted to the PIO and a copy to the Ministry

Not interrupt studies to take up employment; this leads to automatic termination of the scholarship, cancellation of the student visa, and repayment in full of the amount paid for studies, the living allowance and the airfare

HEIs submit quarterly (undergraduate) or monthly (postgraduate) attendance and progress reports for continuation of disbursements; for non-compliance the Ministry reserves the right to recoup money at 25% of monthly stipends
documents: Completed application form, filled in electronically, printed and signed, including the signed Declaration in Section 4
Certified copy of the biodata page of the passport (if available)
Certified copies of educational certificates and transcripts, with certified translations into French or English if the originals are in neither language
Copy of the conditional offer letter from a public Higher Education Institution in Mauritius (if available at time of application) OR copy of receipt from the HEI

Medical certificate duly filled, signed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner in Section 6 of the application form; postgraduate applicants also submit the letter of acceptance from their proposed supervisor(s) and the abridged research proposal
selection_criteria: Selection of candidates is based on merit, having satisfied all conditions attached to the scholarship and upon confirmation from the HEIs that the applicant has been offered a seat
Each nominating agency shortlists and endorses a maximum of fifteen (15) eligible candidates, with the distribution across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes decided by the agency
Postgraduate applicants must have a confirmed seat at the university for consideration of an award at the time of final selection
Candidates who have not been informed of their selection within six months of the MASS application deadline should consider that they have not been selected; individual queries are not encouraged

The final decision to award a scholarship rests with the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and shall be final and binding; the Government reserves the right not to offer any scholarship following the call
coverage: Tuition fees and course-related costs (general/annual fees, miscellaneous fees, laboratory consumables etc) with an annual payment of up to MUR100,000 for SADC beneficiaries and up to MUR160,000 for non-SADC beneficiaries
Part-support of living expenses through a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500, which students are expected to supplement
Return airfare by the most economical route from the country of origin at the beginning of the studies and back to the country of origin after successful completion
Free health care in public hospitals in Mauritius
application_method: Apply for a full-time on-campus programme at a listed public HEI as soon as its application window opens (2026 windows: University of Mauritius, Mahatma Gandhi Institute, Rabindranath Tagore Institute and Polytechnics Mauritius from October 2025; University of Technology Mauritius and Universite des Mascareignes from December 2025; Academy of Design and Innovation from November 2025; postgraduate applicants were asked to apply for a seat by end of January 2026)
Download the relevant application form (undergraduate or postgraduate) from the MASS page, fill it in electronically, print and sign
Submit the completed form and all checklist documents to the nominating agency in your country of citizenship by the deadline that agency determines
The nominating agency endorses Section 5, shortlists up to fifteen candidates and transmits the application forms to the Ministry by 27 March 2026
The Ministry performs the final selection; the host HEI then applies for the student visa and provisional entry permit

On arrival, sign the Scholarship Agreement and submit original certificates within two weeks, complete the medical check-up within one month, open a Mauritian bank account for the allowance, and claim the refund of your one-way air ticket with original receipts
official.application_route: Apply only through the nominating agency in your country of citizenship (applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered), after having applied for or secured a seat at a listed Mauritian public higher education institution.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be resident citizens of member states of the African Union or African Commonwealth countries; Mauritian nationals are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, the scheme is exclusively for non-Mauritian international students: resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No academic field restriction; eligible programmes are full-time on-campus Diploma, Degree, MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes at the listed public HEIs (University of Mauritius, University of Technology Mauritius, Universite des Mascareignes, Mauritius Institute of Education, Mahatma Gandhi Institute, Rabindranath Tagore Institute, Academy of Design and Innovation, Polytechnics Mauritius Ltd), and the application must be routed through the nominating agency of the applicant's country of citizenship.
official.research_requirement: For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, applicants must name their proposed supervisor(s) and upload the written acceptance of the proposed supervisor(s), and must submit an abridged research proposal (title; aims/objectives max 200 words; background and significance max 200 words; methodology and data collection max 300 words; tentative timeframe; equipment/lab/software required; names and contact details of identified supervisors in Mauritius).
official.duration: Maximum duration or minimum course duration, whichever is lesser: Undergraduate Diploma three (3) years; Undergraduate Degree four (4) years; MPhil two (2) years plus 6 months for thesis defence; MPhil/PhD three (3) years plus 6 months for approval of transfer report and one (1) year plus 6 months for thesis defence; PhD three (3) years plus 6 months for thesis defence.
official.description: The Government of the Republic of Mauritius offers the Mauritius Africa Scholarship Scheme to deserving students who are resident citizens of member states of the African Union or African Commonwealth countries, for full-time on-campus diploma, degree, MPhil and PhD programmes tenable at public Higher Education Institutions in Mauritius. The scholarship supports successful candidates in meeting their tuition fees and contributing to their living expenses during their studies in Mauritius, and covers return airfare by the most economical route.
official.english_requirement: Where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination is not English, a valid TOEFL test result with a minimum score of 550 (paper based), 213 (computer based) or 79 (internet based), or valid IELTS test results with a minimum score of 5.5, or an acceptable proof of English Language proficiency; candidates whose language of instruction is not English may be requested to have a verbal interaction virtually prior to the award of the scholarship.

not_confirmed: Applicant-level deadline for the next edition: only the 2026 agency submission date (27 March 2026) is published, and each nominating agency sets its own internal deadline
Exact number of scholarships awarded per country: only the cap of fifteen (15) nominees per nominating agency is published
Tuition fee levels charged by individual public HEIs: only the scheme's annual caps (MUR 100,000 / MUR 160,000) are published
verification.notes: All amounts, caps and conditions were read in full from the official 2026 Call for Applications and the undergraduate and postgraduate Guidelines for Applicants PDFs hosted on the Ministry's MASS page; the MUR 16,500 monthly allowance, fee caps and airfare benefit are identical in both guidelines and match the existing catalogue values.

applicant_utility.summary: MASS is the Mauritian government's scholarship for African nationals with a real but capped package: tuition and course costs paid up to MUR 100,000 (SADC) or MUR 160,000 (non-SADC) a year, a MUR 16,500 monthly living allowance the scheme itself tells you to supplement, and return airfare only once you successfully finish. The decisive step is not the form but the nominating agency in your home country, which endorses at most fifteen candidates, so you need a paid HEI application or conditional offer plus agency clearance well before the Ministry's 27 March 2026 cut-off for the last published edition. Budget for upfront money: you pay your own one-way ticket to Mauritius (refunded on arrival against original receipts) and should land with at least USD 1,000 to cover roughly the first three months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African Union or African Commonwealth citizens aged 18-26 (undergraduate) or under 40 (MPhil/PhD) who hold, or have applied and paid for, a seat at a listed Mauritian public HEI and can win endorsement from their country's nominating agency.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the official List of Nominating Agencies 2026 (33 agencies, e.g. the Federal Scholarship Board in Nigeria, DHET in South Africa, Rwanda's HEC, Egypt's Ministry of Higher Education) and contact that office first; the Ministry will not answer applicant queries.

Apply to a listed public HEI in parallel during its own window (University of Mauritius, Mahatma Gandhi Institute, Rabindranath Tagore Institute and Polytechnics Mauritius from October 2025; University of Technology Mauritius and Universite des Mascareignes from December 2025; Academy of Design and Innovation from November 2025) and keep the conditional offer or the application-fee receipt.
Meet the age test on 01 January 2027 (not yet 26 for undergraduate, not yet 40 for postgraduate) and check your grades against the 21-point A-Level scale or the 60%/12-20 equivalent.
For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD, line up a named supervisor with a written acceptance letter and draft the abridged research proposal in the Ministry's seven-point format before approaching the agency.

Assemble certified copies of birth certificate, passport biodata page, certificates and transcripts (certified French or English translations for anything else), the stamped Section 6 medical certificate, and a certificate of character/morality/good conduct for the visa.
Arrange funds for the one-way arrival ticket plus at least USD 1,000 for the first three months, and confirm no other Mauritian public-source scholarship is held.
common_rejection_risks: Sending the form directly to Mauritius instead of through the nominating agency: applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered at all.
Missing the agency's internal deadline, which is set and announced locally and falls earlier than the Ministry's 27 March 2026 cut-off.
No seat and no proof: without a conditional offer or an application-fee receipt the file is incomplete, and postgraduate applicants must hold a confirmed seat at final selection.
Incomplete forms or missing checklist documents, which the guidelines state will result in disqualification.
Age cut-off breached on 01 January 2027, or already holding an undergraduate degree (degree route), a diploma (diploma route), or a PhD.
Uncertified copies or missing certified translations, and any certificate later found inauthentic, which brings immediate termination after arrival.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: You supplement the MUR 16,500 monthly allowance (the scheme pays it only as part support); you front the one-way arrival ticket (refunded on arrival with receipts) and any return ticket your exit immigration demands; you cover books, overseas fieldwork and data-collection travel including airfare, examination re-sits and repeated years, health and travel insurance, accommodation arranged with the HEI, visits by family or friends, vacation travel, and any fee amount above the annual MUR 100,000 / MUR 160,000 cap.
document_audit: The medical certificate must be completed, signed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner inside Section 6 of the application form itself; a separate unstamped letter does not satisfy the checklist.

Only certified copies are accepted at application stage, but originals of every qualification must be produced within two weeks of arrival and are verified for authenticity; documents not in English or French need certified translations.

Postgraduate files need the supervisor's written acceptance letter and the abridged research proposal in the prescribed seven-point format; a proposed supervisor without written acceptance leaves the application incomplete.
If the passport is not yet available at application time, the biodata page may be omitted, but the passport must be valid for the whole duration of the course before travel.
alerts: The MASS page currently shows only the 2026 edition (call published October 2025, agency submission deadline 27 March 2026), so monitor the MASS page and your nominating agency from around October for the next annual call rather than waiting for Ministry emails.
Each nominating agency may endorse only fifteen candidates in total across undergraduate and postgraduate levels, so the real competition happens inside your home country's agency, not in Mauritius.
Silence means no: candidates not informed within six months of the MASS application deadline should consider themselves not selected, and the Ministry does not respond to individual queries.
Never interrupt studies for employment, anywhere: it triggers automatic termination, visa cancellation and full repayment of tuition paid, the total living allowance and the airfare.

Attendance and progress are actively monitored: quarterly HEI reports (undergraduate) can cost you 25% of your stipend, and failing more than 50% of modules in a semester stops all payments with no arrears later.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit the signed form and checklist documents to your country's nominating agency; the agency endorses Section 5, shortlists up to fifteen candidates and forwards the files to the Ministry; the Ministry decides with the HEIs, after which your host HEI arranges the student visa and provisional entry permit.
